titles.li: The Bell comes for the dead

texts.li: Bell-keepers and sextons of {FACTION} are walking in {PLACE} with spades and bundles of linen, {X_nameDef} at the front. They have come to bury the dead lying on the colony's land.
[lowtech] {FACTION}'s bell-keepers and sextons are walking in {PLACE} with spades over their shoulders and a small bell on every cord. They have come to bury the dead.
[industrial|spacer] {FACTION}'s bell-keepers and sextons are coming in {PLACE} with spades, a handcart of shrouds and their bells. They have come to bury the dead.

settled.li: The Bell's people have made camp {PLACE}: a fire, a lamp, and their spades stacked ready for the morning.
{FACTION}'s sextons have set up camp {PLACE} and marked out where the row of graves will go beyond the wall.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef} of the Bell says the colony's land has given {X_objective} a great deal of work, and asks whether {X_pronoun} might stay and keep its graves.

farewell.li: [buried,claimed] The Bell's people packed their spades and went. Their dead's own people took some of them home, and the rest lie in the row of graves beyond the wall.
[buried,stirred] The Bell's people packed up and left the row of graves beyond the wall. {X_nameDef} rang the bell over it one last time, and said the ground there should be quiet now.
[buried] The Bell's people packed their spades and left. The dead lie in a row of graves beyond the wall, and {X_nameDef} rang the bell over them one last time.
The Bell's people packed up their camp and went back to the road.

lines.li: One more before the light goes.
Wrap this one in the good linen.
The ground keeps what it is given.

momentLines.li: [dig] Start the next one a step to the left.
[bury] Gently, lay this one down slowly.
[ring] Ring once for friend and foe alike.
[stirs] The field is stirring, get the others up.

helpTexts.li: [tales] {A_nameDef} sat by the Bell's fire and heard how they came to bury the dead of the long war.

li.label: Send them wood for the graves (40 wood)
li.tip: One of the colony carries forty wood out to the Bell's camp, for grave boards and the fire.

askTexts.li: {X_nameDef} of the Bell has come to the gate. There are many graves to mark, {X_pronoun} says, and asks whether the colony could spare some wood for the boards.

refused.li: {X_nameDef} says they will mark the graves with stones instead.

outcomes.li: Forty wood is going out to the Bell's camp.

li.label: Send them cloth for the shrouds (20 cloth)
li.tip: One of the colony carries twenty cloth out to the Bell's camp, to wrap the dead before they are buried.

askTexts.li: {X_nameDef} of the Bell has come to the gate. Their linen will not go round all the dead, {X_pronoun} says, and asks for some cloth for shrouds.

refused.li: {X_nameDef} says they will bury them in what they wore.

outcomes.li: Twenty cloth is going out to the Bell's camp.

titles.li: Tamers on the way to the fair

texts.li: Tamers of {FACTION} are walking in {PLACE} with their animals, {X_nameDef} at the front. They will mark out a ring with torches and hold a bout there every afternoon.
[ws:fair] On their way to {SITUATION}, tamers of {FACTION} are walking in {PLACE} with their animals. They will hold a bout every afternoon at their ring.

settled.li: The Circuit's tamers have made camp {PLACE}, with a ring marked out by torches beside their tents.
{FACTION}'s tamers have pitched their tents {PLACE} and set torches round a ring of trampled grass, ready for the afternoon's bout.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef} of the Circuit says the colony's hands are as good with animals as anyone on the road, and asks whether {X_pronoun} might stay and learn from them.

farewell.li: [champion] The tamers pulled up their torches and went on to the fair. Before they left, {X_nameDef} tied the Circuit's token on the arm of the colony's best challenger.
[fought] The tamers pulled up their torches and went on to the fair, talking about the colony's challengers all the way to the road.
The tamers pulled up their torches and went on to the fair.

lines.li: Keep your eyes on the animal, not on me.
Win their trust and they will win your battles.
To be beaten fairly is an honour.
Who is next in the ring?

momentLines.li: [challenge] Step into the ring when you are ready.
[spar] Good, again, and lower this time.
[won] Well fought, that was a fair win.
[lost] Not this time, but you kept your feet.
[champion] This token is yours, you earned it in the ring.

helpTexts.li: [show] {X_nameDef} put two of the Circuit's animals through their paces by the ring, and {A_nameDef} watched the whole thing.
[tales] {A_nameDef} sat with the tamers by their fire and heard how Nessa Pell found the egg in the crater.

li.label: Send {A_nameDef} to challenge in this afternoon's bout
li.tip: {A_nameDef} goes to the ring and takes on one of the tamers' animals in a friendly bout, as the Circuit's tamers do. Who wins depends on {A_possessive} handling and melee. Two challengers a day at most. One bout in twenty-five, the animal's blow lands and leaves a bruise.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} is going over to the ring for this afternoon's bout.

li.label: Send feed for their animals (30 raw food)
li.tip: One of the colony carries thirty raw food out to the tamers' camp for their animals.

askTexts.li: {X_nameDef} of the Circuit has come to the gate. The animals are hungry after the road, {X_pronoun} says, and asks whether the colony could spare some feed for them.

refused.li: {X_nameDef} says they will let the animals graze a little further out.

outcomes.li: Thirty raw food is going out to the tamers' camp.

ColonyCouncil.CampKindDef.label: Wheel's yard
ColonyCouncil.CampKindDef.leavesWhy: a yard on wheels packs everything it builds back onto its carts and takes it on to the next stop

texts.li: The yard of {FACTION} is rolling in {PLACE} with its carts and pack animals, {X_nameDef} walking in front. They will set up a scrap market and a mending tent for three days.
[lowtech] {FACTION}'s yard is rolling in {PLACE} with creaking carts piled high with scrap and tools. They will trade and mend things for three days.
[industrial|spacer] {FACTION}'s yard is rolling in {PLACE}, carts and trailers loaded with scrap, tools and spare parts. They will trade and mend things for three days.

settled.li: The Wheel's yard has set up {PLACE}: carts in a ring, a mending tent, and scrap laid out on tarpaulins for sale.
{FACTION}'s yard has unloaded {PLACE}, and the fixers already have the mending tent open.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef} of the yard says {X_pronoun} has had enough of the road for a while, and asks whether the colony could use someone who can fix almost anything.

farewell.li: [stayed,mended] The yard packed everything back onto its carts and rolled on, a few days later than it meant to. The colony's mended things are back where they belong.
[sour] The yard packed up and rolled on. The fixer who argued over the price did not say goodbye.
[mended] The yard packed everything back onto its carts and rolled on, after mending what the colony brought them.
The yard packed everything back onto its carts and rolled on to the next stop.

lines.li: Buy it cheap, sell it better.
If it rolls, it comes with us.
We'll have that running by supper.

momentLines.li: [haggle] That price is fair, and you know it.
[haggle] I'm not mending it for nothing, friend.
[stay] We'll stay a couple of days longer, the trade here is good.

helpTexts.li: [mend] {X_nameDef} came over from the yard and mended {COUNT} {THING} of the colony's for nothing.
[tales] {A_nameDef} sat by the yard's fire and heard about the night their valley burned.

li.label: Have the yard mend our worn clothes and weapons
li.tip: One of the yard's fixers goes round the colony's worn clothes and weapons, in its stores and on its people, and mends each back to whole. The price is about a third of what the wear has taken off their worth, carried out to the yard.

outcomes.li: One of the yard's fixers is coming over to mend the colony's worn things, and the silver is going out to the yard.

li.label: Sell them our scrap
li.tip: The colony's slag and broken clothes and weapons are carried out to the yard, and the yard pays for them in silver.

outcomes.li: The colony's scrap is going out to the yard, and the yard is paying for it.

li.label: Send wood for their forge (40 wood)
li.tip: One of the colony carries forty wood out to the yard for their forge.

askTexts.li: {X_nameDef} of the yard has come to the gate. Their forge is running low, {X_pronoun} says, and asks whether the colony could spare some wood.

refused.li: {X_nameDef} says they will burn what scrap wood they have.

outcomes.li: Forty wood is going out to the yard.
